speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing a psychiatric condition along with a new onset movement disorder; to help me understand your situation, could you please describe what you mean by the movement disorder and how long you have had these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the background; it seems you are on risperidone for two months. You mentioned a new movement disorder—could you describe the specific movements you are experiencing (e.g., stiffness, tremor, twitching, or restlessness) and when they started relative to starting the medication?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms you are describing—specifically the inability to remain still, fidgeting, and leg crossing/un-crossing—are classic signs of akathisia. Did these symptoms start shortly after you began taking the risperidone, and does the discomfort feel like it is in your whole body or just in your legs?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: College student, lives with parents. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-induced Akathisia secondary to Risperidone.

Your symptoms of inner restlessness, pacing, and fidgeting began after starting risperidone and are classic signs of this side effect.
